title: Urgent fixes without stopping the roadmap
subtitle: A CI/CD redesign for complex projects and time-sensitive customer work.

blocks.text: We built a simple CI/CD workflow so this B2B SaaS team could stay flexible: urgent customer fixes can now ship independently while larger projects continue on their own schedules. The core insight of the project is about properly setting up automated git tags, release branches, and image registries.

blocks.alt: Diagram of the deployment and release identity flow

blocks.text: The previous pipeline featured a common DevOps setup: it deployed everything merged into main through a moving latest container image. Shipping one fix meant shipping all the work in progress so far, which is fine for single-headed developments, but could mean delaying another release or taking unfinished changes into production when there are multiple projects going on in parallel. Rollback meant manual intervention in AWS.
Version tags had been tried before, but they named the source code without reliably identifying the image being deployed, a common issue when the production image is simply labeled “latest”.
It was like a bank issuing numbered tickets, then throwing them away after the first desk. At the cashier, everyone is just “next.” You can no longer reliably tell who has already been checked.

I led the DevOps redesign around one principle: keep that identity all the way through. We built immutable container images identified by their commit SHA, then promoted the same QA-tested images to production. A release registry recorded every deployment.

Release branches let us cherry-pick urgent fixes without including unrelated work. Each patch still went through testing. We built the core pipeline in about ten working days alongside ongoing product work.

This solution will last because it is easier to maintain and totally automated, not because it is safer. Anyone pressured by competing priorities and tight deadlines will look for the shortest path to immediate success, so the architecture has to take all the friction away from whoever is executing the process.
Automated git tags invoked by a skill-command to deploy a hotfix provide that path, which means anyone with zero experience in software deployments can ship urgent code to production.
